title: a top-level accessor read carries the accessor's unsatisfied capability and is refused by name
notes: specification/requirements.mdx, 'Inference': "Requirement inference MUST be transitive through ordinary calls." specification/type-system.mdx, 'Fallibility Inference': R is inferred from `Capability.context()` calls and transitive callees. Reading a get-accessor CALLS the accessor — there is no syntax that names one without running it — so an accessor access is an ordinary call and charges the accessor's requirement row. specification/requirements.mdx, 'Satisfaction': "When the compiler knows the complete closure, an unsatisfied capability MUST be a compile error." A top-level accessor read is a top-level call, so it is refused exactly as a top-level method call with the same row is. Before 2026-08-25 the reference reported SMITHERS1802 here — the wrong code with the right instinct — and the Go fork accepted the program outright. `messageContains` names the capability because code and position alone are satisfied by a refusal naming the WRONG requirement; the bare nominal name is declared rather than a row rendering, which the two backends legitimately format differently.
